message.content:
The Battle of Waterloo (18 June 1815) was one of the bloodiest single-day battles in European history.  Casualty figures vary depending on the source and how “casualties” are defined (killed, wounded, missing, captured).  A commonly cited estimate is:

| Side | Approximate casualties |
|------|------------------------|
| French (Napoleon’s army) | ~25 000–30 000 (killed, wounded, missing) |
| Anglo‑Dutch & Prussian (Allied forces) | ~20 000–25 000 (killed, wounded, missing) |

These totals include both killed and wounded, as well as soldiers who were taken prisoner or went missing.  Some historians give slightly lower or higher numbers, but the consensus is that roughly 45 000–55 000 troops were affected on both sides combined.
